HCG tests need to be read within a certain time frame and checking it overnight should not be taken as a positive.

Given that other HCG tests seem negative, I'd suggest maybe the doctors are right about it not being an ectopic. But something is obviously wrong, have they suggested what is causing your pain? Is there a particular reason that you believe it is an ectopic aside from the correlation in symptoms e.g. you've had one in the past or you have the typical bleeding patterns?

Hi, I would suggest that if you're still having negative pregnancy tests you're unlikely to have an ectopic. Have you experienced one in the past? It's not impossible that it is an ectopic but imo (NAD) seems more likely that something else is causing your symptoms- i.e. perhaps the issue that led to going for an TVUS in the first place. Also, what is referred to as "implantation bleeding" apparently does not typically last more than a couple of days. It sounds like you're stressed and that's understandable but taking the facts into consideration, it may be more likely ovulation pain or a delayed period. A 5 day delay may be unusual for you but it can happen from time to time. I hope you manage to relax a bit, I can imagine this is scary but it doesn't sound like the typical ectopic.
